lesson.title: Continuous Gym
lesson.subtitle: ik ben aan het werken, zij zit te lezen, hij staat te wachten

hook.title: Four Postures, One Continuous
hook.content: Zitten, staan, liggen, lopen: four posture verbs, four ways to picture an action in progress. The te + infinitive is the constant.

pattern.title: Posture + te + infinitive
pattern.content: Ik zit te lezen, hij staat te wachten, zij ligt te slapen, wij lopen te praten. The posture verb is finite; the action infinitive closes the sentence.
pattern.trap_note: The posture verb is not a tense marker; it adds a physical image. Use aan het + infinitive when no posture is implied.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Continuous Gym):
exercises.target_answer: zitten, staan, liggen, lopen, lezen, werken
exercises.meaning: to sit, to stand, to lie, to walk, run, to read, to work
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Continuous Gym": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.
“Ik zit te lezen.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Continuous Gym”.
“Hij staat te wachten.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — Posture + te + infinitive.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: The posture verb is not a tense marker; it adds a physical image. Use aan het + infinitive when no posture is implied.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
exercises.explanation: “Zij ligt te slapen.” is word-for-word “She lies to sleep.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: Posture + te + infinitive.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: We are walking and talking.
exercises.explanation: “Wij lopen te praten.” reuses only material taught in “Continuous Gym” — Posture + te + infinitive.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Wij lopen te praten.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising Posture + te + infinitive.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I am working.”
twist.explanation: Without a posture, use aan het + infinitive: aan het werken.

summary.outcome: Choose a posture verb or aan het for an action in progress.
summary.takeaway: The continuous is a picture plus an infinitive; the posture is optional colour.
summary.curiosity_teaser: Up next on De Brug: Dutch Idioms & Directness.

zitten.etymology_derivation: English sit and Dutch zitten are the same verb; s voiced to z.

staan.etymology_derivation: English stand and Dutch staan are the same verb.

liggen.context_translation: The book lies on the table.
liggen.etymology_derivation: English lie and Dutch liggen are the same verb.

lopen.etymology_derivation: English leap is the same old verb; Dutch narrowed it to walking or running.

lezen.etymology_derivation: English read and Dutch lezen are the same verb; the d became z in Dutch.

werken.etymology_derivation: English work and Dutch werken are the same verb.
